text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Moslem-Croat federation House of Representatives adopts law on modifying boundaries of municipalities divided by inter-entity or cantonal lines. The draft law still must be approved by the federation House of People.
- Croat representatives walked out of the parliamentary session complaining that the draft law was pushed through by a Moslem majority.

- The Moslem-Croat federation and Serb republic have prepared an agreement on trade between the entities. Federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic expects the agreement to be signed by trade ministers of both entities next Wednesday.

- The opposition Social-Democratic Party (SDP) says it will refuse to cooperate with the implementation of the Dayton peace accord if Serb authorities fail to release SDP deputy, Ivan Mijacevic, who was recently arrested.
- The executive board of Bosnian-German car company TAS- Volkswagen AG announces meeting to discuss destiny of stripped car factory in Sarajevo suburb of Vogosca.
- Egypt will help open an orphanage in Mostar for war victims with a donation worth more than one million dollars, newspaper reports. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
